title: Nifty closes 0.84% higher, cooling off from intraday highs - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
Markets reopened after the Diwali break with a bang on Wednesday, but couldn’t hold on.

The Nifty 50 surged to an intraday high of 25,424, before giving back nearly half its gains as hotter-than-expected US inflation data revived fears of an aggressive Federal Reserve rate hike in December, pulling the index to close at 25,255.05, up 210.40 points or 0.84 per cent.

The Sensex settled at 81,879.40, gaining 772.75 points or 0.95 per cent, well below the 1,300-point surge seen in early trade.

The Nifty has now gained around 11.1 per cent across 10 sessions, its ninth consecutive winning regular session, powered by FII inflows of roughly ₹54,000 crore in the first nine days of November, equivalent to about $5.68 billion, the strongest monthly inflow since September 2024.

Vikram Kasat, Chief Business Officer – Advisory and Dealing at PL Capital, said sustained FII inflows, earnings momentum and stable crude prices would be important for the market’s next leg. He advised investors to favour fundamentally strong stocks rather than chase sharp rallies.

Sectoral performance was split. PSU banks, auto, chemicals and FMCG led gains, while IT, realty and pharma came under selling pressure, with Vinod Nair, Head of Research at Geojit Investments, noting that “the rupee’s recent appreciation, combined with expectations of higher-for-longer global rates, weighed on IT stocks.” The broader market held up better: the Nifty Midcap 100 gained 0.81 per cent and the Smallcap 100 outperformed sharply, rising 1.59 per cent. Bank Nifty closed at 60,792.40, up 1,051.15 points or 1.76 per cent, after touching 61,394 intraday before profit-booking set in.

Among individual movers, Kalyan Jewellers jumped 12 per cent on strong quarterly results, though a one-time property-sale gain flattered its profit figures.

Cochin Shipyard fell sharply as margins thinned, this came the same day the Ministry of Defence signed a ₹498.58 crore contract with Cochin Shipyard for the refit and re-powering of INS Betwa, replacing its steam propulsion with a diesel-engine system.

Moody’s raised India’s FY27 GDP growth forecast to 7 per cent from 6.5 per cent, citing broad-based economic momentum and the possibility of a new private capex cycle.

On the macro front, Brent crude traded near $92–93 per barrel, while WTI hovered at $86–87. The Indian rupee firmed to 93.6 against the dollar, drawing support from FII inflows and softer crude, though the dollar’s post-CPI rebound capped gains. India VIX ticked up slightly to 17.55.

US October CPI rose 0.4 per cent month-on-month, above the 0.3 per cent expected, cementing a 25-basis-point Fed hike at the December FOMC meeting in market pricing, with a 15 per cent probability of 50 basis points.

Globally, Anthropic’s Nasdaq IPO, set to price on November 18 at $70–$78 per share, valuing the AI company at up to $1.4 trillion, is drawing investor attention.

Markets face a data-heavy Thursday: India’s October CPI inflation, US weekly jobless claims, UK Q3 GDP and crude oil inventory figures are all due, alongside quarterly earnings from HAL, Oil India, NMDC, Alkem Laboratories and Vodafone Idea, among others.

“Whether renewed risk appetite holds will depend on the inflation and PPI data, which together should shape the outlook for domestic prices and global interest rates,” Nair said. Ajit Mishra, SVP at Religare Broking, sees the 24,800–25,000 zone as a potential buying opportunity, with 25,500–25,750 as the next upside target.
